Confusable pairs across the three teen license levels, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
Level One has two time phases: in the first six months driving is limited to 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., and after that any hour is allowed, but a supervising driver is required in both phases. [A01]
Why it matters: group levels; difficulty medium; confusable with Level Two unsupervised hours.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A02
A Level Two license holder may drive unsupervised between five a.m. and nine p.m., and at any hour when traveling straight to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency medical organization in which they serve [A02].
Why it matters: group levels; confusable with Level One hours.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
The Level One holding period is nine months, while the driving log needs at least 60 hours with 10 at night; these are different requirements that both apply before Level Two. [A01]
Why it matters: group levels; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
A Level Two Limited Provisional License must be held for at least six months before applying for a Full Provisional License [A02].
Why it matters: group levels; confusable holding periods.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
The front-seat rule belongs to Level One: only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front. [A01]
Why it matters: group passengers; confusable with Level Two passenger limits.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
The Level Two passenger limit counts under-21 passengers from outside the household when driving unsupervised; household members alone have no limit, except they cannot ride with under-21 non-household passengers. [A02]
Why it matters: group passengers; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A02
The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits, yet a driver under 18 still may not use a cell phone except for listed emergency calls. [A02]
Why it matters: group phones; confusable full provisional versus no rules.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A03
For a provisional licensee the alcohol rule is any amount, not a blood alcohol limit, and a conviction means a one-year revocation. [A03]
Why it matters: group alcohol; prereq alcohol section; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A04
Under Lose Control, Lose Your License, a student loses their license for twelve months upon receiving a suspension for more than ten consecutive days or a disciplinary assignment to an alternative educational setting for more than ten consecutive days [A04].
Why it matters: group school; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A04
If your driver license has a restriction, you may drive only within the limits of that restriction; otherwise the law treats you as driving without a license [A04].
Why it matters: group restrictions; prereq licensing section.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]
